title: Beyond the ANA: Centromere, Topoisomerase I, Ro/La and U1RNP
summary: Match anti-centromere and anti-topoisomerase I to limited and diffuse systemic sclerosis, learn why anti-La almost never appears without anti-Ro, and see why anti-U1RNP supports mixed connective tissue disease only at high titre with overlapping clinical features.

reviewer.note: Teaches Ch. 53 Hits 4, 5 and 13 and Exam Trap 5. Checked against Yang 2020 and Kayser 2015 (systemic sclerosis antibodies), Yoshimi 2012, Franceschini 2017 and Negrini 2022 (Ro/La), and Reiseter 2017, Alves 2020 and Chaigne 2018 (MCTD), all full text via Europe PMC. Qualified: Hit 4 percentages (57–82% of CREST, 75% of dcSSc) were not found; the sources give whole-cohort frequencies and note anti-centromere outside SSc and anti-topoisomerase I in limited disease (register flag rv-ssc-aca-ata-context). Hit 13: Sharp 1972 described 25 patients, not 20, anti-RNP had not been high in all of them on later review, and in a nationwide prospective cohort conversion went to SLE and RA more often than to SSc (rv-mctd-sharp-evolution). Hit 5 and Trap 5 are supported; sensitive multiplex assays report isolated anti-La more often (rv-isolated-la-assay). Not taught: CREST letters, Ro/La prevalence figures and the Number Vault table.

objectives: Match anti-centromere and anti-topoisomerase I antibodies to limited and diffuse systemic sclerosis and their typical organ risks.
Explain why anti-La almost always occurs with anti-Ro and how to handle an anti-La-positive, anti-Ro-negative result.
State what defines mixed connective tissue disease and why a positive anti-U1RNP alone does not make the diagnosis.

scenes.title: Three panels, three stories
scenes.altText: Invented scenario: three extractable nuclear antigen (ENA) results reach the immunology bench. (1) A woman with years of Raynaud phenomenon and tight skin on the fingers only: centromere pattern on HEp-2, anti-CENP-B positive. (2) A man with rapidly spreading skin thickening on the trunk and a dry cough: anti-topoisomerase I (anti-Scl-70) positive. (3) A woman with dry eyes and mouth: a bead multiplex panel reports anti-La/SSB positive, anti-Ro60 and anti-Ro52 negative. Question token: “Which result should make you look twice?”

cues.text: Three antibody panels reach the bench. A woman with years of Raynaud phenomenon and tight skin on her fingers has a centromere pattern and anti-centromere antibodies.
A man with skin thickening spreading up his trunk and a dry cough is positive for anti-topoisomerase one. And a woman with dry eyes and mouth is anti-La positive, but anti-Ro negative.
Each result points somewhere. Which one should make you look twice?

props.label: Which result should make you look twice?

scenes.title: Two scleroderma antibodies, two paths
scenes.altText: Schematic: two antibody cards for systemic sclerosis (SSc). Anti-centromere (ACA): targets centromere proteins, CENP-B the main target; seen as a centromere pattern on HEp-2 IIF; about 20–38% of SSc cohorts; associated with limited cutaneous SSc (CREST), long-standing Raynaud phenomenon and pulmonary arterial hypertension without fibrosis; better prognosis; also reported in SLE, primary biliary cholangitis, Sjögren syndrome and Raynaud phenomenon. Anti-topoisomerase I (ATA, historically anti-Scl-70, named after a 70 kDa band that proved to be a breakdown product of the 100 kDa protein): about 15–42% of SSc, specificity 90–100%; associated with diffuse cutaneous SSc, interstitial lung disease (even in limited disease), heart involvement and worse prognosis. Shared token: both are highly predictive of SSc in patients with Raynaud phenomenon.

cues.text: Two antibodies split systemic sclerosis into two paths. Anti-centromere antibodies target centromere proteins, mainly CENP-B, and light up as a centromere pattern on HEp-2 cells.

They go with limited cutaneous disease, the CREST picture: long-standing Raynaud phenomenon and pulmonary arterial hypertension without fibrosis, and a better prognosis. They are not exclusive: they also turn up in lupus, primary biliary cholangitis and Sjögren syndrome.

Anti-topoisomerase one, the old anti-Scl-70, is very specific for systemic sclerosis. It goes with diffuse skin disease, interstitial lung disease, heart involvement and a worse prognosis. The 70 in the name was a breakdown fragment of a larger protein.
In a patient with Raynaud phenomenon, either antibody is highly predictive of developing systemic sclerosis.

props.label: Raynaud + either antibody → high risk of SSc

scenes.title: Ro walks alone, La walks with Ro
scenes.altText: Schematic Ro/La particle: Ro60 bound to small hY RNAs, with La in the same ribonucleoprotein (RNP) system; Ro52 drawn apart, labelled “separate system” (a direct Ro52–Ro60 interaction was not confirmed). Card 1: anti-Ro can occur alone in many sera; anti-La is usually accompanied by anti-Ro; anti-La-positive, anti-Ro-negative patients are rare. Card 2: in mice, immunising with La induces anti-Ro60 and immunising with Ro60 induces anti-La (intermolecular epitope spreading across the complex). Card 3: the 2016 ACR/EULAR primary Sjögren classification criteria count anti-Ro only; isolated anti-La was excluded for lack of specificity; highly sensitive multiplex assays frequently report isolated anti-La, which complicates interpretation. Token: anti-Ro/La can be present despite a negative IIF ANA.

cues.text: Ro sixty sits in a ribonucleoprotein particle with small Y RNAs, in the same antigen system as La. Ro fifty-two is a separate antibody system: it can be found without anti-Ro sixty.
Anti-Ro is often found alone, but anti-La usually comes with anti-Ro. In mice, immunising with La triggers antibodies to Ro sixty, and the reverse, so the response can spread across the complex.

So a patient positive for La but negative for Ro is rare. The 2016 Sjögren classification criteria count anti-Ro only and left out isolated anti-La because it lacks specificity. Very sensitive multiplex assays report isolated anti-La more often, which makes it hard to interpret.
One more catch: anti-Ro and anti-La can be present even when the immunofluorescence ANA is negative, so a negative screen does not end the search when Sjögren syndrome is suspected.

scenes.title: Anti-U1RNP and mixed connective tissue disease
scenes.altText: MCTD card: defined by high-titre anti-U1 ribonucleoprotein (anti-U1RNP) antibody PLUS overlapping features of two or more of systemic sclerosis, SLE, polymyositis and rheumatoid arthritis (puffy hands, Raynaud phenomenon, arthritis, myositis). Sharp and colleagues described it in 1972 in 25 patients. Specificity card: anti-RNP is not exclusive to MCTD; it occurred in 35% of one group’s SLE patients, and in one population study only 18.9% of anti-RNP-positive patients met any MCTD criteria. Course card: no agreed classification criteria (Sharp, Kasukawa, Alarcón-Segovia, Kahn); in a Norwegian cohort 14 of 118 patients converted over a mean disease duration of 17 years (6 to SLE in the results [5 in the paper’s discussion], 4 to RA, 3 to SSc, 1 to antisynthetase syndrome); conversion figures differ widely between MCTD cohorts, from none reported in one cohort to 42.1% in another. Hook answer card.

cues.text: Mixed connective tissue disease is defined by a high titre of anti-U1 ribonucleoprotein antibody together with overlapping features of systemic sclerosis, lupus, myositis or rheumatoid arthritis, such as puffy hands, Raynaud phenomenon, arthritis and myositis.
Anti-U1RNP alone is not the diagnosis. One group found it in about a third of lupus patients, and in one population study fewer than one in five anti-RNP-positive patients met any MCTD criteria.

There are four competing criteria sets and no agreed one. Some patients evolve: in a Norwegian cohort, fourteen of one hundred and eighteen converted, to lupus and rheumatoid arthritis more often than to systemic sclerosis.

Back to the hook: the centromere and topoisomerase results fit their pictures. The anti-La-positive, anti-Ro-negative result is the one to look at twice: it is uncommon, and assays differ in how they detect Ro and La, so interpret it with care.

scenes.title: Three classic traps
scenes.altText: Three trap cards: “Anti-La positive, anti-Ro negative is a typical Sjögren result” (✓ rare; anti-La usually comes with anti-Ro; the 2016 criteria count anti-Ro only); “Anti-centromere means diffuse disease with lung fibrosis” (✓ anti-centromere = limited disease, PAH; anti-topoisomerase I = diffuse disease, lung fibrosis); “Positive anti-U1RNP = MCTD” (✓ needs high titre plus overlapping clinical features; anti-RNP also occurs in SLE and other diseases).

cues.text: Trap one: anti-La without anti-Ro is a typical Sjögren result. No: it is rare. Anti-La usually travels with anti-Ro, and the 2016 criteria count anti-Ro only.
Trap two: anti-centromere means diffuse disease with lung fibrosis. No: centromere goes with limited disease and pulmonary hypertension; topoisomerase one goes with diffuse disease and lung fibrosis.
Trap three: any positive anti-U1RNP means mixed connective tissue disease. No: it needs a high titre plus overlapping clinical features, and anti-RNP is common in lupus too.

props.title: ✗ “La + / Ro − is typical.”
lines: ✓ Rare: La usually comes with Ro

scenes.title: Ro can solo, La tags along
scenes.altText: Memory aid: “Ro can solo, La tags along with Ro. CENtromere keeps it contained (limited); topo spreads wide (diffuse skin, lungs). U1RNP mixes the party, but only a big crowd plus mixed guests makes MCTD.” Tokens: Ro can solo · La tags along · topo spreads wide. A card lists where the aid breaks.

cues.text: Memory aid: Ro can solo, but La tags along with Ro. Centromere keeps it contained and limited; topo spreads wide, into diffuse skin and the lungs. And U1RNP mixes the party, but only a high titre plus mixed clinical features makes MCTD.

Where it breaks: sensitive multiplex assays can report La without Ro; anti-topoisomerase one also occurs in limited disease; anti-centromere occurs outside scleroderma; and Ro fifty-two follows its own rules.

scenes.title: Takeaway
scenes.altText: Two tokens: “Anti-La almost always with anti-Ro · La + / Ro − = look twice”, “Centromere = limited · topo I = diffuse + lung · U1RNP high titre + overlap = MCTD”.

cues.text: Anti-La almost always comes with anti-Ro, anti-centromere points to limited and anti-topoisomerase I to diffuse systemic sclerosis with lung fibrosis, and anti-U1RNP supports mixed connective tissue disease only at high titre with overlapping clinical features.

props.label: Anti-La almost always with anti-Ro · La + / Ro − = look twice
Centromere = limited · topo I = diffuse + lung · U1RNP + overlap = MCTD

explanation.what: Plain language: after a positive ANA screen, labs identify the exact target of the antibody. Two targets split scleroderma into a milder, limited form and a more aggressive diffuse form. In Sjögren syndrome, one antibody (anti-Ro) often appears by itself, but its partner (anti-La) almost never appears without it, so La on its own is a result to double-check. A third antibody (anti-U1RNP) is the hallmark of an overlap disease, but many people with it have other diseases. Scientific terms: extractable nuclear antigen (ENA), anti-centromere antibody (ACA; CENP-B), anti-topoisomerase I antibody (ATA; anti-Scl-70), limited and diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis (lcSSc, dcSSc), CREST, pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), interstitial lung disease (ILD), Ro60/SSA, Ro52/TRIM21, La/SSB, hY RNA, ribonucleoprotein (RNP), intermolecular epitope spreading, 2016 ACR/EULAR classification criteria, anti-U1 small nuclear RNP (anti-U1RNP), mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD), disease conversion.
explanation.why: Systemic sclerosis antibodies are largely tied to distinct clinical subsets, so the specificity predicts which organs are at risk. Ro60 and La belong to one RNP antigen system and the antibody response can spread across the complex, which is why anti-La is usually accompanied by anti-Ro; Ro52 is a separate system. MCTD was defined from a combination of an antibody and overlapping clinical features, and anti-RNP alone lacks specificity.
explanation.measure: ACA: about 20–38% of SSc (Kayser 2015) or 20–57.8% (Yang 2020); ATA: 15–42% of SSc with specificity 90–100% (Kayser 2015). Anti-Ro and anti-La in Sjögren syndrome: 70–100% and 40–90% (Yoshimi 2012; a later passage of the same review gives 35–70% for anti-La) or 33–74% and 23–52% (Negrini 2022), depending on assay and cohort. MCTD: Sharp 1972 described 25 patients; anti-RNP in 35% of one group’s SLE patients; 18.9% of 264 anti-RNP-positive patients met any MCTD criteria; conversion 14 of 118 over a mean 17-year disease duration (Reiseter 2017); across MCTD cohorts reviewed by Alves 2020, conversion ranged from none reported to 42.1%.
explanation.differs: ACA (limited, PAH, better prognosis) vs ATA (diffuse, ILD, worse prognosis); anti-Ro alone (common) vs anti-La alone (rare, assay-sensitive); anti-Ro60 vs anti-Ro52 (separate system); anti-U1RNP positivity vs MCTD (antibody plus overlap features).
explanation.examAngle: Expect: which antibody goes with limited versus diffuse scleroderma or with lung fibrosis, the suspicious La-positive Ro-negative result, and the antibody that defines MCTD.

takeaway: Anti-La almost always comes with anti-Ro, anti-centromere points to limited and anti-topoisomerase I to diffuse systemic sclerosis with lung fibrosis, and anti-U1RNP supports mixed connective tissue disease only at high titre with overlapping clinical features.

questions.stem: A woman with dry eyes and dry mouth has a bead multiplex ENA panel that is anti-La/SSB positive but anti-Ro60 and anti-Ro52 negative. What is the best interpretation?

options.text: An uncommon, assay-dependent pattern that should be interpreted with caution
options.rationale: Correct. Anti-La is usually accompanied by anti-Ro; La-positive, Ro-negative results are rare, highly sensitive multiparametric assays frequently detect isolated anti-La, and assays differ in anti-Ro and anti-La detection.

options.text: The typical serology of primary Sjögren syndrome
options.rationale: Incorrect. Anti-Ro is the typical finding, alone or with anti-La; isolated anti-La is uncommon.

options.text: Enough to meet the antibody item of the 2016 ACR/EULAR Sjögren criteria
options.rationale: Incorrect. The 2016 criteria count anti-Ro only; isolated anti-La was excluded for lack of specificity.

options.text: Proof of an error, because anti-La can never occur without anti-Ro
options.rationale: Incorrect. Isolated anti-La is rare, not impossible; the result needs careful interpretation, not automatic rejection.

questions.stem: A man with rapidly progressive skin thickening of the trunk and arms develops interstitial lung disease. Which autoantibody is most likely?

options.rationale: Correct. Anti-topoisomerase I is associated with diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis, interstitial lung disease and a worse prognosis.
Incorrect. Anti-centromere is associated with limited cutaneous disease, pulmonary arterial hypertension without fibrosis and a better prognosis.
Incorrect. Anti-La is a Sjögren syndrome and lupus antibody, not a systemic sclerosis subset marker.
Incorrect. Anti-U1RNP is the defining antibody of mixed connective tissue disease, not of diffuse systemic sclerosis.

questions.stem: Which finding is required, together with overlapping clinical features of systemic sclerosis, lupus, myositis or rheumatoid arthritis, to define mixed connective tissue disease?

options.rationale: Correct. MCTD is defined by high-titre anti-U1RNP together with overlapping features of two or more of these diseases.

options.text: Any positive anti-U1RNP, without clinical features
options.rationale: Incorrect. Anti-RNP is not specific: it is common in lupus, and most anti-RNP-positive patients do not meet MCTD criteria.
Incorrect. Anti-centromere points to limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis.
Incorrect. Isolated anti-La is a rare, assay-sensitive finding, not a marker of MCTD.

claims.text: Anti-centromere (CENP-B, centromere pattern) with limited cutaneous SSc, Raynaud, PAH and better prognosis, also outside SSc; anti-topoisomerase I (anti-Scl-70 misnomer) highly specific, with diffuse disease, ILD, heart involvement and worse prognosis; both predictive of SSc in Raynaud phenomenon.

Ro60/hY RNA particle, Ro52 a separate system; anti-Ro often alone, anti-La usually with anti-Ro; epitope spreading across the complex in mice; 2016 criteria count anti-Ro only; multiplex assays report isolated anti-La more often.
Anti-Ro/La can be present despite a negative immunofluorescence ANA.

MCTD defined by high-titre anti-U1RNP plus overlap features; Sharp 1972, 25 patients; anti-RNP not specific (35% of one SLE group; 18.9% of anti-RNP-positive patients meet MCTD criteria); no agreed criteria; conversion 14/118 (6 SLE, 4 RA, 3 SSc, 1 antisynthetase); conversion differs widely between MCTD cohorts.

Reviewer specifics: anti-centromere in 57–82% of CREST and up to 85% of lcSSc; anti-Scl-70 in 75% of dcSSc; anti-centromere in up to 25% of idiopathic Raynaud; “all 20 original Sharp cases”; MCTD evolving “most often” into scleroderma; CREST letter expansion.
claims.note: Not taught; not found, or given differently, in the sources read.

claims.text: Scenario invented; Ro/La particle and antibodies shown schematically.
“Ro can solo, La tags along; topo spreads wide.”

accuracyFlags.issue: Ch. 53 Hit 4 equates anti-centromere with limited cutaneous SSc/CREST (57–82% of CREST) and anti-Scl-70 with diffuse SSc (75% of dcSSc). Kayser 2015 and Yang 2020 support the subset associations but give whole-cohort frequencies (anti-centromere 20–38% or 20–57.8% of SSc; anti-topoisomerase I 15–42% or 14–71%), note anti-centromere in SLE, primary biliary cholangitis, Sjögren syndrome and Raynaud phenomenon, and anti-topoisomerase I in limited disease with ILD risk even there; the reviewer’s subset percentages were not found (register flag rv-ssc-aca-ata-context).

Ch. 53 Hit 13 says high-titre anti-U1RNP was found in all 20 original Sharp et al. 1972 cases and that MCTD patients most often evolve into scleroderma. Alves 2020 states Sharp described 25 patients and that on later review anti-RNP levels had not in fact been high in all of them; in Reiseter 2017, 14 of 118 patients converted, six to SLE (five in the paper’s discussion), four to RA, three to SSc and one to antisynthetase syndrome, and Alves 2020 shows conversion differing widely between MCTD cohorts (register flag rv-mctd-sharp-evolution).

Ch. 53 Hit 5 and Exam Trap 5 (anti-La almost never without anti-Ro) are supported by Yoshimi 2012, Franceschini 2017 and Negrini 2022, but Franceschini 2017 notes that highly sensitive multiparametric assays frequently detect isolated anti-La and that assays differ in anti-Ro and anti-La detection, so how rare the pattern looks depends on the method (register flag rv-isolated-la-assay).

morphology.note: No images; antibodies, the Ro/La particle and results shown as schematic cards.
